In [[machine learning]], '''multi-epoch training''' is the practice of feeding a model the same training data multiple times (epoches).

According to experiments ran by [[Source:Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models (Conference paper)|name-author]], result from repeating the same training data up to 4 times is comparable to training entirely from fresh data for the same total token count.<ref>{{#cite:Q3174}}</ref>

=== Mathematical modelling ===

[[File:Multi-epoch training and loss function.png|thumbnail|450px|In experiments conducted by [[Source:Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models (Conference paper)|name-author]], 4 epochs multi-epoch training produced nearly identical result to single epoch training with the same amount of total tokens. (only $0.5%$ more loss).]]
Let

* $D$ = '''corpus size''': the number of '''unique''' tokens available for training,
* $R$ = number of repetitions,
* $R^{\ast}$ = '''repetition ceiling parameter''', to be determined experimentally

For any given model architecture, the efficacity of a '''multi-epoch training''' with $R$ epochs can be measured by the amount of fresh data required to produce equivalent result, known as the '''effective corpus size''' $D_\text{eff}$.

[[Source:Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models (Conference paper)|name-author]] experimentally determined:

$$
D_{\text{eff}}
= D\!\left(1+R^{\ast}\!\left(1-e^{-R/R^{\ast}}\right)\right).
$$

==== Finite ceiling ====

[[File:Multi-epoch training data budget and performance.png|thumbnail|450px|left]]
As $R\to\infty$,

$$
D_{\text{eff}}\to D(1+R^{\ast}),
$$

so repetition can raise effective corpus size only up to a finite limit.

According to experimental results from [[Source:Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models (Conference paper)|name-author]], $R^* \approx 15$ for natural language corpus.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3174}}</ref>
